headline: Set rent conditions for two 536 Emmett Street apartments and let rent increases at 83-85 Atkins Avenue stand.
summary: Hearings covered rent increase requests at several Emmett Street and Atkins Avenue units. Rent at 536 Emmett Street, Apt A-6 will rise $10.00 once identified issues are remedied, and Apt A-2 stays at $1,300 until repairs are completed. The hearings for 519 and 523 Emmett Street and 103 Caesar Drive were continued, and the 90 Gridley Street hearing was moved to next month.
decisions: Approved the amended minutes of the August 26, 2026 meeting, all in favor.
Approved a $10.00 rent increase for 536 Emmett Street, Apt A-6, once identified issues are remedied, all in favor.
Approved keeping rent at $1,300 per month for 536 Emmett Street, Apt A-2, until repairs are remedied, with 24/7 storage access added, all in favor.
Moved the hearing for 90 Gridley Street to next month by agreement of both parties.
Continued the hearing for 103 Caesar Drive to next month because notice to the landlord was not confirmed.
Continued the hearing for 519 Emmett Street to the October meeting, all in favor.
Continued the hearing for 523 Emmett Street to the October meeting, all in favor.
Found the proposed rent increase at 83-85 Atkins Avenue for Marc Blaskow not harsh and unconscionable, so the increase stands, all in favor.
Found the proposed rent increase at 83-85 Atkins Avenue for Michelle Cruz not harsh and unconscionable, so the increase stands, all in favor.
Approved October 28, 2026 as the next meeting date, all in favor.

plain_text:
FAIR RENT COMMISSION 
September 23, 2026 at 6:00 PM  
Bristol City Hall 
111 N. Main Street, Bristol, CT 
MINUTES 
 NAME PRESENT ABSENT 
COMMISSIONERS Anthony Lozier (T) – Chairman  X  
 Brian Brady (H) X  
 Cristina Costa (T) X  
 Susan Pyzynski (H)  X 
 Debra Schur (L) X  
 Nick Palmer (L) X  
 Kimberly Gendron (T) Alternate X  
 Kimberly Ploszaj (H) Alternate X  
    
COUNCIL LIASION Erick Rosengren X  
MAYOR Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu X  
STAFF Attorney Jonathan Donovan, Asst. Corp. 
Counsel 
X  
 Maria Theam, Corporation Counsel’s Office X  
Note:  H (Homeowner Representative) L (Landlord Representative) T (Tenant Representative) 
1. Call To Order 
The meeting was called to order at 6:07 p.m. 
2. Introduction of Commissioners 
The commissioners introduced themselves. 
3. Seating of Alternates 
The alternates Kimberly Gendron and Kimberly Ploszaj were seated in place of two 
commissioners who recently resigned.   
4. Discussion and Approval of minutes of August 26, 2026 and take any action as necessary. 
MOTION TO APPROVE the amended minutes of the August 26, 2026 meeting by Anthony Lozier, 
Seconded by Cristina Costa.  All in favor, none opposed.  Motion carries.
5. Hearings in the matters of:  
 
MOTION to Consolidate the first two hearings of Pauline Cabrila and Robert C. Hardy and Bristol 
Meadows LLC by Anthony Lozier and seconded by Cristina Costa.  All in favor, none opposed.  
Motion carries.   
 
a. Pauline Cabrila (Tenant) and Bristol Meadows LLC (Landlord) 536 Emmett Street, Apt 
A-6, Bristol, Connecticut. 
Pauline began her five-minute testimony and expressed concerns regarding the 
condition of her apartment, as well as her desire to retain her storage area. She stated 
that she did not believe a rent increase was warranted due to the issues she identified 
and the lack of improvements to the unit. 
Dawn S., representing the landlord, spoke on the landlord’s behalf. She stated that 
representatives visited Pauline’s unit in August and reviewed each of the concerns 
Pauline had raised. According to Dawn, the landlord offered to address the identified 
issues and also offered Pauline the option of relocating to another unit. Dawn stated 
that Pauline indicated she would be willing to remain in her current unit in its existing 
condition if there were no rent increase. It was noted that Pauline has resided in the 
unit for approximately 30 years and had declined the offer of a new vanity and stove. 
Dawn also stated that Pauline is grandfathered in with respect to her storage area. 
Following the initial testimony, both the tenant and landlord were provided two 
minutes for rebuttal and participated in the two-minute questioning period of one 
another. The Commissioners then asked additional questions of both the tenant and 
landlord. 
Nick Palmer made a motion that, effective July 1, 2026, the current rent remain 
unchanged until the issues identified in the report are remedied. The motion was 
seconded by Brian Brady. 
The motion was amended to provide that, once the identified issues are remedied, the 
rent shall increase by $10.00.  All in favor, none opposed, Motion Carries.   
b. Robert C. Hardy (Tenant) and Bristol Meadows LLC (Landlord) 536 Emmett Street, Apt 
A-2, Bristol, Connecticut.  
 
Robert C. Hardy provided testimony regarding concerns with his apartment and storage 
area. He stated that he has resided in the building for approximately four and a half 
years and that his rent has increased annually. He raised concerns regarding the 
condition of his bathroom ceiling, which he stated is peeling. He also discussed the lack 
of designated handicapped parking and noted that he has a handicap following a hip
replacement. Mr. Hardy expressed concern regarding an additional $25.00 rent increase 
this year. 
 
Dawn provided testimony on behalf of the landlord and discussed the landlord’s 
perspective. She stated that Mr. Hardy’s rent has increased by a total of $225 since the 
beginning of his tenancy and that the parties were able to reach a resolution through 
mediation following a previous complaint. She noted that Mr. Hardy’s current rent 
remains lower than the rents being charged to new tenants entering the building. Dawn 
also stated that Mr. Hardy’s unit is considered a “renovated unit,” having been 
renovated within approximately the last five to six years. In response to the issue of a 
veteran’s discount, Dawn stated that she did not believe the company currently offers 
one. She also addressed the storage area and stated that the storage room is kept 
locked due to previous safety concerns. 
Anthony Lozier made a motion that the rent remain at $1,300 per month until the 
repairs identified in the Building Official’s report are remedied. Once the identified 
repairs have been completed, the landlord may implement the proposed rent increase. 
Nick Palmer proposed that the motion also include a provision requiring the tenant to 
be provided with 24/7 access to the storage unit. The motion, including the additional 
provision regarding storage access, was seconded by Nick Palmer. All were in favor, 
none opposed, and the motion carried. 
c. Joseph and Eric Testman (Tenants) and Marieanne St. Germain (Landlord) 90 Gridley 
Street, Bristol, Connecticut. 
 
This hearing was moved to next month by agreement of both parties prior to tonight’s 
meeting.  
 
d. Jamie Nadeau, Scott Nadeau and Nicole Miller (Tenants) and Chelsea Ho Thuan 
(Landlord) 103 Caesar Drive, Bristol, Connecticut 
 
This hearing is continued to next month as notice to landlord has not been confirmed.   
 
e. Gerard Gaudreau and Nicole Gaudreau (Tenants) and Kevin Dumont / Jacob 
Properties LLC (Landlord) 519 Emmett Street, Bristol, Connecticut. 
 
Motion to Continue this case to October meeting or under the agreement from this 
evening is approved by Anthony Lozier and Seconded by Cristina Costa.  All in favor, 
none opposed.  Motion carries.  
 
f. Alison Gonzalez (Landeen) (Tenant) and Kevin Dumont / Jacob Properties LLC 
(Landlord) 523 Emmett Street, Bristol, Connecticut. 
Motion to Continue this case to October meeting or under the agreement from this 
evening is approved by Anthony Lozier and Seconded by Cristina Costa.  All in favor, 
none opposed.  Motion carries.
Anthony Lozier made a motion to consolidate the two Atkins hearings. The motion was 
seconded by Cristina. All were in favor, and the motion carried. 
A motion was made to allow both complainants to testify, with one respondent 
providing testimony on behalf of the landlord. The motion was seconded by Nick 
Palmer. All were in favor, none opposed, and the motion carried. 
g. Marc Blaskow (Tenant) and Jerry Gonsalves (Landlord) 83-85 Atkins Avenue, Bristol, 
Connecticut 
Ida Opacity, Power of Attorney for Marc Blaskow, appeared on his behalf regarding the 
proposed rent increase. She stated that Marc was upset upon receiving notice of the 
increase and discussed concerns regarding how the increase may affect him. She noted 
that Marc is currently under the care of a psychologist and receives Section 8 housing 
assistance. 
Ms. Opacity also raised questions and concerns regarding the ownership of the property 
and indicated that she believed there may be issues surrounding the identity of the 
property owner. She stated that her primary concern is protecting the interests and 
well-being of her nephew, Marc. 
h. Michelle Kaminski Cruz (Tenant) and Jerry Gonsalves (Landlord) 83-85 Atkins Avenue, 
Bristol, Connecticut 
Michelle Cruz appeared and was sworn in. She provided testimony regarding her 
concerns with the proposed rent increase and stated that she has resided at the 
property for approximately 30 years. Ms. Cruz also raised questions regarding the 
ownership of the property and requested legal documentation confirming that Jerry is 
an owner, noting that she had previously always dealt with Jim. 
Ms. Cruz also discussed concerns regarding the condition and safety of the property. 
She referenced prior issues with the stairs and stated that she was unsure whether 
those issues had been corrected. She also expressed concerns regarding the safety and 
condition of the decks. 
 
James Gonsalves appeared and was sworn in. He provided testimony regarding the rent 
increases and stated that Michelle Cruz’s rent has increased by a total of approximately 
$125 over the past 28 years. He stated that his brother would like to sell the properties 
and increase the rents and confirmed that Jerry is a co-owner of the property. 
Mr. Gonsalves discussed rental rates at other properties they own, including two 
additional three-bedroom properties. He stated that the lowest rent currently charged 
for those units is approximately $1,600 per month, with rents for other units reaching 
approximately $2,000 per month.
Regarding Marc Blaskow, Mr. Gonsalves stated that he had not previously been 
informed that correspondence or documentation concerning Marc should be directed to 
Ida Opacity rather than Marc. He further stated that he had not seen the Power of 
Attorney documentation prior to the hearing. Mr. Gonsalves also addressed Marc’s 
Section 8 housing assistance and stated that the proposed rent increase should be 
directed to the tenant rather than Section 8. 
Michelle Cruz provided rebuttal testimony and reiterated her concerns regarding the 
ownership of the property, stating that she remained unclear as to who the landlord or 
property owner is. She also stated that Section 8 has been dealing with her for years and 
that Mr. Gonsalves was aware of this. Ms. Cruz stated that she had provided the 
relevant documentation to Jerry. 
Mr. Gonsalves also expressed concerns regarding the expenses associated with the 
properties and stated that he is currently losing money. 
Marc Blaskow – Anthony Lozier made a motion to find that the proposed rent increase 
is not harsh and unconscionable and that the rent increase shall stand. The motion was 
seconded by Cristina Costa. All were in favor, none opposed, and the motion carried. 
Michelle Cruz – Anthony Lozier made a motion to find that the proposed rent increase is 
not harsh and unconscionable and that the rent increase shall stand. The motion was 
seconded by Cristina Costa. All were in favor, none opposed, and the motion carried. 
6. Discussion by commissioners of old business and take any action as necessary. 
a. proposal to allow the commissioner to grant a continuance 
 
Motion to discuss the new rules and procedures by Anthony Lozier and seconded by 
Nick Palmer.   All in favor, none opposed.  Motion carries.  Anthony passed out 
information that was prepared by Attorney Donovan for all commissioners to review 
and discuss at the next meeting.   
 
7. Discussion by commissioners of new business and take any action as necessary. 
There was some discussion of the alternates and two commissioners who resigned and 
who will take their place.   
 
8. Discussion by commissioners of meeting dates and agendas and take any action as necessary. 
a. Next Meeting: October 28, 2026 at 6:00 PM, City Hall. 
Motion to Adopt October 28, 2026 as their next meeting date by Anthony Lozier and 
seconded by Cristina Costa.  All in favor, none opposed.  Motion carries.  
 
9. Public participation 
There was no public participation.   
 
10.  Adjournment. 
Motion to Adjourn at 8:05 p.m. by Anthony Lozier and seconded by Cristina Costa.  All in favor, 
none opposed and the meeting was adjourned.
